```{r cars}
# Save results because downloading is very long

if (!file.exists("data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")) {
  # Store the project ID
  projectid = 'cnz-data-warehouse-d66eb552a5'
  
  # Set your query
  sql = 'SELECT mpan, interval_start, consumption_kwh FROM `cnz-data-warehouse-d66eb552a5.src_cosy.heatpump`'
  
  # Run the query; this returns a bq_table object that you can query further
  tb <- bq_project_query(projectid, sql)
  
  # Store the data in a tibble
  consumption_data <-bq_table_download(tb, n_max=Inf, bigint="integer64", page=250000)
  unique_consumption_data <- unique(consumption_data, by = c("mpan", "datetime"))
  
  # Save
  saveRDS(unique_consumption_data, "data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")
  
} else {
  consumption_data <- readRDS("data/scratch/smart_meters.RDS")
}

```

```{r}

# load agreement data to know when they switched to cosy
# this part could be improved by adding which tariff they are on 
# I have been ignoring that people can switch back to non cosy

if (!file.exists("data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")) {
  agreement_data <- fread("data/input/Cosy Agreement.csv") 
  
  # Step 2: Collapse Overlapping Agreements
  agreement_data_collapsed <- agreement_data %>%
    mutate(cosy = ifelse(product_display_name=="Cosy Octopus",1, 0)) %>% # Create cosy dummy
    arrange(mpan, hashed_meter_point_id, cosy, is_variable, agreement_valid_from) %>% # sort by id, cosy, Time of Use and start if agreement
    group_by(hashed_meter_point_id, mpan, cosy, is_variable) %>% # collapse to keep data on cosy/tou
    mutate(collapse_group = cumsum(agreement_valid_from != lag(agreement_valid_to, default = first(agreement_valid_from)))) %>%
    group_by(mpan, hashed_meter_point_id, cosy, is_variable, collapse_group) %>%
    summarise(agreement_valid_from = min(agreement_valid_from),
              agreement_valid_to = max(agreement_valid_to)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    arrange(mpan, agreement_valid_from) %>%
    group_by(mpan) %>%
    mutate(overlap_flag = ifelse(agreement_valid_from < lag(agreement_valid_to,  #check there is no double counting
                                                            order_by = agreement_valid_from, 
                                                            default = first(agreement_valid_from)), 1, 0),
           duration = as.numeric(difftime(agreement_valid_to, agreement_valid_from, units = "days"))) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(agreement_collapsed_id = row_number())
  
  rm(agreement_data)
  
  # Convert your data frames to data.table objects
  agreement_data_collapsed <- as.data.table(agreement_data_collapsed)
  consumption_data <- as.data.table(consumption_data)
  
  # Convert the relevant columns to POSIXct to handle date-times
  agreement_data_collapsed[, agreement_valid_from := as.POSIXct(agreement_valid_from)]
  agreement_data_collapsed[, agreement_valid_to := as.POSIXct(agreement_valid_to)]
  consumption_data[, interval_start := as.POSIXct(datetime)]
  
  # Ensure the mpan columns are of the same type (character)
  agreement_data_collapsed[, mpan := as.character(mpan)]
  consumption_data[, mpan := as.character(mpan)]
  
  
  # Step 1: Adjusted non-equi join to merge by mpan and datetime >= agreement_valid_from
  result <- consumption_data[agreement_data_collapsed, 
                             on = .(mpan, interval_start >= agreement_valid_from, interval_start < agreement_valid_to),
                             .(mpan, interval_start, datetime, consumption_kwh, hashed_meter_point_id, 
                               cosy, is_variable, 
                               agreement_valid_from, agreement_valid_to),
                             nomatch = 0, allow.cartesian = TRUE]
  
  
  # Filter agreement_data_collapsed where agreement_valid_to is NA
  agreement_data_NA_to <- agreement_data_collapsed[is.na(agreement_valid_to)]
  
  # Identify consumption_data not in result
  consumption_not_in_result <- consumption_data[!result, on = .(mpan, datetime)]
  
  # Merge filtered agreement_data_collapsed with non-merged consumption_data
  consumption_not_in_result <- consumption_not_in_result[agreement_data_NA_to, on = .(mpan, interval_start >= agreement_valid_from), 
                                                         .(mpan, interval_start, datetime, consumption_kwh, hashed_meter_point_id, 
                                                           cosy, is_variable, 
                                                           agreement_valid_from, agreement_valid_to),
                                                         nomatch = 0, allow.cartesian = TRUE]
  
  # Append this merge to the original result
  final_merge <- rbind(result, consumption_not_in_result, fill = TRUE)
  
  # check uniqueness
  unique_rows <- uniqueN(final_merge, by = c("mpan", "datetime"))
  
  # Display the result
  head(final_merge)
  rm(consumption_data, consumption_not_in_result, agreement_data_NA_to, agreement_data_collapsed, result, unique_rows)
  gc()
  
  final_merge[, time_since_cosy := fifelse(cosy == 1, 
                                           floor(as.numeric(difftime(datetime, agreement_valid_from, units = "weeks"))), 
                                           NA_integer_)]
  final_merge[, hour := hour(datetime)]
  
  # Step 3: Assign rate_period with conditional logic
  final_merge[, rate_period := fcase(
    hour >= 4 & hour < 7, "Morning Cosy",
    hour >= 13 & hour < 16, "Afternoon Cosy",
    hour >= 16 & hour < 19, "Peak Rate",
    default = "Other"
  )]
  
  saveRDS(final_merge, "data/scratch/smart_meters_merged.RDS")
  
  # Aggregate the data
  aggregated_data <- final_merge[, .(total_consumption = sum(consumption_kwh)), 
                                 by = .(mpan, rate_period, cosy, date, time_since_cosy)]
  
  rm(final_merge)
  saveRDS(aggregated_data, "data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")
} else {
  aggregated_data <- readRDS("data/scratch/aggregated_data.RDS")
}

```
## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r, echo=FALSE}

# Prepare data for line plot (aggregate by month)
monthly_data <- aggregated_data %>%
  mutate(month = floor_date(date, "month")) %>%
  group_by(month) %>%
  summarise(monthly_consumption = mean(total_consumption))

# Line Plot
ggplot(monthly_data, aes(x = month, y = monthly_consumption)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(title = "Monthly Consumption Over Time", x = "Month", y = "Total Consumption") +
  theme_minimal()


```

``` {r}
# Prepare data for bar chart
cosy_data <- aggregated_data %>%
  group_by(cosy, rate_period) %>%
  summarise(total_consumption = mean(total_consumption))

# Line Plot
ggplot(cosy_data, aes(x = as.factor(cosy), y = total_consumption, fill = as.factor(cosy))) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  labs(title = "Consumption by Period with Cosy", x = "Rate Period", y = "Total Consumption") +
  theme_minimal() +
  facet_grid(~rate_period)
```

```{r}
etable(feols(total_consumption ~ as.factor(cosy) | date + mpan, 
             data = aggregated_data, 
             cluster = ~mpan, 
             split = ~ rate_period))

```

```{r}

# filter for panel
tt <- aggregated_data %>% 
  group_by(mpan) %>% 
  mutate(week = week(date)) %>% 
  summarise(start = min(date), min_week=min(week), max_week=max(week), count= n()) %>% 
  mutate(share_obs = count/3164) %>%
  filter(start < (as.Date("2022-12-13") - weeks(15)),
         share_obs > 0.5)


# Fixed-effects regression
est_did <- feols(total_consumption ~ + i(weeks_since_cosy, -1) | date + mpan, 
                 data = aggregated_data %>% filter(mpan %in% tt$mpan, weeks_since_cosy>-15, weeks_since_cosy<15),
                 split =~ rate_period,
                 cluster = ~mpan)

# Now we can plot the result of the interaction with coefplot
etable(est_did)

coefplot(est_did)
coefplot(est_did[2], title="Effect on total consumption - Morning Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[1], title="Effect on total consumption - Afternoon Off Peak Cosy")
coefplot(est_did[3], title="Effect on total consumption - Peak rate")
coefplot(est_did[4], title="Effect on total consumption - Other rate")


```



```{r}
etable(feols(total_consumption ~ as.factor(cosy) | date + mpan, 
             data = aggregated_data %>% group_by(mpan, date, cosy) %>% summarise(total_consumption=sum(total_consumption)), 
             cluster = ~mpan))

```

```{r}
# Prepare data
aggregated_data_prepared <- aggregated_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(weeks_since_cosy)) %>%
  mutate(weeks_recoded = case_when(
    weeks_since_cosy < -10  ~ -10,
    weeks_since_cosy > 10   ~ 10,
    TRUE                    ~ weeks_since_cosy
  )) %>% group_by(mpan, date, weeks_recoded) %>% summarise(total_consumption=sum(total_consumption))

# Fixed-effects regression
est_did <- feols(total_consumption ~ + i(weeks_recoded, 0) | date + mpan, 
                 data = aggregated_data_prepared %>% filter(weeks_recoded > -10 ) %>% filter(weeks_recoded < 10), 
                 cluster = ~mpan)

# Now we can plot the result of the interaction with coefplot
coefplot(est_did)
```
